content.title: About
content.content: Halibut is a flatfish of the family Pleuronectidae that inhabits the cold northern waters of the Pacific and Atlantic oceans. Wild‑caught halibut is harvested in its natural environment and flash‑frozen immediately, preserving its authentic flavor, texture, and nutritional qualities.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Halibut can grow over 2 m in length and weigh more than 200 kg.
It is one of the most valuable commercial fish species in North America and Japan.
The flesh has a firm yet tender texture with a mild, slightly sweet taste.
Freezing occurs within 24 hours of capture, locking in high levels of omega‑3 fatty acids.
In the wild, halibut migrates long distances in search of feeding grounds.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Halibut provides EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Around 20 g of complete protein per 100 g helps with tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D contributes to bone strength and immune function.

items.title: Minerals: selenium and iodine
items.content: Selenium protects cells from oxidative stress, while iodine supports thyroid health.

items.title: Low mercury content
items.content: Compared with larger predatory fish, halibut contains relatively low levels of heavy metals.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including halibut.

items.title: Sodium in pre‑seasoned products
items.content: If the fish is pre‑salted, consider the overall sodium intake.

items.title: Thorough cooking required
items.content: Raw or undercooked fish may harbor parasites; cook to an internal temperature of 63 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Halibut can be baked, pan‑seared, steamed, or used in sushi and salads. Thaw it in the refrigerator, pat dry, then season with salt, pepper, lemon, or herbs before cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen halibut at –18 °C or lower. Once thawed, use within 1–2 days and store in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C. Do not leave the fish at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
